Subject: Data locality & lifecycle alignment for Redwood marketplace listing

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this — we’re finalizing our marketplace procurement checklist and have a handful of specific asks around data locality, retention, and deletion that must align with our security policy. Attaching our template for reference. High-level questions:

1) When our customers route traffic through the Redwood marketplace listing, can data be constrained to a single cloud region (e.g., us-west-2) for both inference requests and logs/backups?
2) What are your default retention windows for request logs, KV caches, and object snapshots? Any on-demand purge API?
3) If a customer requests account deletion, what is the timeline and steps to remove all PII from live services, backups, and any offsite snapshots?
4) Do you support customer-managed KMS keys per tenant in the marketplace flow?
5) For cross-region failover, are backups ever replicated outside the selected cloud provider or region by default?
6) What evidence/artifacts do you provide for audit (deletion confirmation, S3/GCS/Azure blob deletion events, snapshots purge logs)?

We’d like concise answers we can feed into our procurement/security review. If easier, happy to hop on a 30-min sync.

Thanks —
Emily Ross
Head of Cloud Security, NimbusApps

Emily —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers at a high level so your procurement team has something to work with; happy to expand any point or join a call. I’ve attached a short region & flow diagram.

1) Region locking: For marketplace listings we offer region pinning at the customer level. Requests and inference artifacts (request metadata, KV cache) are routed to the pinned region (we support AWS/GCP/Azure equivalents). Logs can be kept within the region; we default to same-region storage unless the customer opts into cross-region analytics.

2) Retention windows (defaults): request logs 30 days; KV cache entries are ephemeral (session-based) and flushed on idle; object snapshots (model checkpoints/backups) default to 90 days in cold storage. We can adjust these via contract for enterprise customers.

3) Deletion flow: we perform a three-step process — logical deletion (immediate), scheduled secure purge (default 30 days), and permanent purge of cold snapshots (up to 90 days). We provide an API/portal request path for accelerated deletion where supported.

4) KMS: marketplace flow supports customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) on AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault for object encryption and snapshot encryption; there are some integration steps in the onboarding doc.

5) Cross-region backups: by default we do not replicate backups across cloud providers. For geo-resilience customers can enable cross-region replication within the same provider (e.g., AWS us-west-2 -> us-east-1), but cross-cloud replication is not the default and requires explicit configuration.

6) Audit artifacts: we can provide deletion manifests, storage-level deletion events (S3/GCS/Azure blob delete logs), and an audit export (signed) for compliance reviews.

Proposed next step: short zoom with you + legal to map the specific DPA language we would add to the marketplace listing and confirm any stricter snapshot purge SLA. Available tomorrow 10:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Partner Solutions (Marketplace) — Redwood Inference

Emily —

Thanks — below are the clarifications you can share with legal. I’ve kept them explicit so they can be translated into contract language:

• Scope of the 30-day scheduled secure purge: this applies to live service data (inference request logs, metadata stores, and tenant-level config). Cold snapshots (model checkpoints and backups stored in archival buckets) follow the snapshot lifecycle described separately (default 90 days). We do not consider snapshots part of the "live" 30-day purge window.

• Snapshots vs. daily backup archives: snapshots (application-level model checkpoints) are retained by default 90 days before permanent purge. Daily backup archives (infrastructure snapshots) are retained per the backup profile — default 30 days for hot backups, 90 days for cold archives. We do not keep any snapshot/archive beyond 365 days without an explicit contract clause.

• Cases where cold snapshots could exceed 90 days: only under customer request and with explicit contractual terms (we can add a retention-exception clause).

• BYOK in marketplace: yes — tenant-level requirement for BYOK is supported. Customers can mandate use of their KMS keys during onboarding; we surface this as a required field for the marketplace listing. When BYOK is selected, Redwood does not hold the key material and any snapshot encryption/decryption relies on the customer-managed key.

• Cross-cloud replication: not enabled by default. Replication is always an opt-in configuration and will be documented in the listing with the replication topology.

• Evidence for audit: we provide a deletion manifest (signed JSON) with timestamps, storage-level deletion events (S3/GCS/Azure activity logs) and an operation summary. For added assurance we can run a quarterly attest audit and provide redacted proofs on request.

Next steps from Redwood side:
- Marissa will draft a DPA annex that defines retention, purge windows, BYOK behavior, and audit artifacts for marketplace customers.
- Ben will confirm snapshot purge mechanics with infra (exact S3/GCS/Azure lifecycle transition timings and cold-tier purge processes) and update the draft.
- Priyom will coordinate a short review call with NimbusApps and legal — propose 2026-10-21 10:30 PT.

If that works for you, I’ll get a calendar invite out and share the draft annex link.

Best,
